newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 9.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Following allegations that sculptor Anthony-Noel Kelly was using body parts to create his art works, police have raided his South London studio. Forensic scientists are now attempting to identify the discovery of up to 30 dismembered human corpses.
- BOOM WARNING BACK TO HAUNT THE CHANCELLOR

During this pre-election period the word 'boom' has become commonplace on Conservative party posters and in ministerial speeches, much to the consternation of Chancellor Kenneth Clarke who warned earlier this parliament that 'this Chancellor does not want a boom because boom gets followed by bust.'At tomorrow's meeting with the Bank of England the Chancellor is expected to argue strongly that base rates need to increase by at least a quarter of a point.
The US dollar hit a new four year high against the yen. A Japanese government minister insisted that the country's interest rates would stay low.
- OZ GREEN LIGHT FOR FOREIGN BANK TAKEOVERS

The Wallis Committee report released by Australian Treasurer Peter Costello has stated that any future foreign takeover would now be assessed on an individual case basis. The wide ranging report of the country's financial system has scrapped the ban on foreign takeovers of Australia's four largest banks.
- 717 STG COLONIAL LISTING SPARKS A UK DILEMMA

A choice is given to Australian mutual Colonial Group policyholders (of which there are 250,000) - they can sell their free shares into a public offer or wait for the May 19th debut of the 1.5bn stg (717 stg) stockmarket listing. 78 million shares are being released in Britain.
